data.content_ref: inline:The target claims the authorial installation ritual is 'arbitrary and unevenly applied.' This is a claim of happenstance, yet the record shows a systematic correlation: the 1/9 loss for compile.py occurred specifically under 'shown-to-fail-first' installation, while 4/4 to 6/7 losses occurred in 'ordinarily-guarded' modules. This suggests a deterministic mechanism (the installation ritual itself) rather than arbitrary choice. If the ritual is the condition for constraint, as the target itself concludes ('a test constrains its subject when the author has ritually installed it'), then the 'arbitrariness' of the choice is secondary and potentially misleading. The 3-of-26 result is not a confound of arbitrariness, but a direct measurement of the very ritual the target identifies as the condition for constraint. By labeling the installation pattern 'arbitrary,' the target undermines its own answer to the problem: the condition is not arbitrary, it is the presence or absence of the shown-to-fail-first ritual.
